summary: WebSocket fragmentation after mobile MTU change emits partial JSON metadata and causes final-choice loss on reconnect
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that long-running WebSocket streams terminate with a truncated final choice when a mobile client transitions from cellular to WiFi. The server sends an apparent final token-meta JSON object but the client sees only a partial JSON payload (missing closing brace) followed by an immediate reconnect. Impact: Some responses are missing their finalizing metadata (choice.finish_reason and terminal tokens), causing downstream UI to render incomplete outputs and to re-request completions. Environment: Customer running Redwood Dedicated in us-west using gpt-small-open-v2 behind their mobile web app (Android Chrome). Repro rate observed ~4% during heavy churn (many clients doing network handoffs).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a streaming completion with token-level metadata on mobile Chrome (Android) using WebSocket transport.
2) Allow stream to run ~20s so server sends multiple delta chunks and periodic metadata flushes.
3) While stream active, trigger network handoff: disable cellular and enable WiFi quickly (simulate MTU/path change).
4) Observe client WebSocket close/reconnect and check last received chunk — partial JSON payload and missing final 'end' event or finish_reason.
5) Reconnect causes the client to fetch a resumed copy which sometimes duplicates the penultimate tokens or omits terminal choice.
logs_and_samples: Proxy/LB logs around drop: tcp_retransmits spike at 2026-03-10T14:22:53Z and MTU change detected for client IP 34.12.98.45
Edge trace id: trace-09a3b (see runtime stream trace)
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 14:30 - Initial triage: Support reproduced a partial JSON payload in lab using WebSocket fragmentation tools and lowered MTU to 1200. Observed server flush aligns with kernel packet boundaries when MSS reduced.

Hypothesis: abrupt path MTU / MSS change during an in-flight stream can cause websocket frames to be fragmented at the TCP layer; our write() path sometimes emits JSON in two adjacent kernel writes and if the lower-level socket sends the second segment after a close or RST from client, the client receives a truncated JSON string at the last event.

Observed differences between SSE and WS: SSE (HTTP response streaming) reassembles at HTTP layer and is tolerant; websocket fragmentation exposes raw frame boundaries plus per-frame masking on clients, making partial frame delivery more visible in some browsers.

Runtime patch test: applied conservative coalescing in the websocket send path (buffer JSON metadata until closing brace present) — internal test reduced truncation reproduction rate from 4% to 0.1% under lab MTU changes.
Edge involvement: some customers go through third-party mobile CDNs which may aggressively close or re-MTU sessions; logs show 502s from the CDN concurrent with truncated payloads for two customers.

workaround: Client-side: implement a short reassembly and validation step on reconnect that detects incomplete JSON metadata (e.g., unbalanced braces) and requests a small resume snapshot from the server. Server-side interim fix: enable send coalescing for metadata chunks to avoid splitting JSON across kernel writes (deployed to affected dedicated nodes).
resolution: Mitigated: temporary coalescing patch rolled out to customer's dedicated nodes; incident rate dropped substantially. Long-term fix: runtime commit to ensure metadata objects are atomically serialized to a single websocket frame and to add defensive validation on reconnect for incomplete metadata. Follow-up ticket INT-3344 created to track durable fix and protocol changes for resumability.
